statement.p: Find a vector parametric equation for the line perpendicular to the surface z = 5 x^2 + 3 y^2 at the point (-2,-2,32).

static.solution: f(x,y,z) = 5 x^2 + 3 y^2 - z. Then the surface z = 5 x^2 + 3 y^2 is a level surface of f at the value 0. The gradient of f is perpendicular to the level surface. \nabla f(-2,-2,32) = (10 x\,\vec i + 6 y\,\vec j - \vec k)\bigg|_{(-2,-2,32)} = -20\,\mathit{\vec i}-12\,\mathit{\vec j}-\,\mathit{\vec k}. So a possible parameterization is \vec r(t) = -\left(2+20t\right)\,\mathit{\vec i}-\left(2+12t\right)\,\mathit{\vec j}+\left(32-t\right)\,\mathit{\vec k}.
